skill.description: Guides agents to use Daem0nMCP memory tools for session briefings, context checks, decision records, and outcome tracking.

skill.author: DasBluEyedDevil

security_audit.summary: The static external command detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline MCP tool examples, not shell execution. Semantic review found overbroad agent control, persistent memory writes, automatic spec import, and broad codebase indexing guidance that can expose project context without explicit consent.

remediation.issue: Overbroad mandatory instructions can override user intent.
remediation.suggestion: State that user, system, and tool policies take priority, and ask for consent before automatic MCP calls.

remediation.issue: Persistent memory writes may capture sensitive project context.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact secrets and confirm before storing file paths, rationale, decisions, or outcomes.

remediation.issue: Broad codebase indexing lacks scope controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval and path limits before indexing a repository or analyzing impact.

remediation.issue: OpenSpec auto-import can persist private requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Make spec import opt-in and document where imported data is stored and how it can be deleted.

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions often lose context, repeat mistakes, or skip decision tracking. This skill defines a Daem0nMCP workflow for briefings, checks, memories, and outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to check for Daem0nMCP tools before using the protocol.
Requires a session briefing with past decisions, warnings, patterns, and Git changes.
Prompts context checks and file recall before code changes.
Defines memory categories for decisions, patterns, warnings, and learnings.
Explains graph memory linking, tracing, and visualization workflows.
Describes code indexing, semantic code search, and impact analysis tools.
limitations: Only applies when Daem0nMCP tools are installed and exposed to the agent.
Does not provide the MCP server implementation or tool schemas.
Can create persistent memories, so users should review sensitive content before use.
Uses strict workflow language that may need local policy alignment.

use_cases.title: Preserve Coding Context
use_cases.description: Use session briefings and memory checks before changing important files.

use_cases.title: Capture Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Record design choices, rationale, and outcomes for later sessions.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP Memory Workflows
use_cases.description: Create a consistent process for context checks, memory links, and graph review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Daem0nMCP Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the daem0nmcp-protocol skill. Check whether Daem0nMCP tools are available, then brief me on relevant memories before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for a File Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Before editing the files I name, run the recommended context checks and summarize any warnings that affect the change.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Design Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: After we choose an approach, record the decision, rationale, related file, and expected outcome using the Daem0nMCP workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Memory Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace the memory chain for this feature, identify superseded decisions, and show which prior outcomes should influence the implementation.

output_examples.input: Review Daem0nMCP context before editing authentication code.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the briefing status, relevant warnings, and file memories that affect the planned authentication change.

output_examples.input: Record the database pooling decision after implementation.
output_examples.output: The assistant stores the decision, captures rationale, and later records whether the implementation worked.

output_examples.input: Show relationships around the authentication redesign.
output_examples.output: The assistant requests a memory graph and summarizes related decisions, superseded approaches, and open conflicts.

best_practices: Confirm user consent before persisting sensitive project details in memory.
Run context checks before edits that change behavior or architecture.
Record outcomes after testing so future sessions can learn from results.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets, credentials, or private customer data in memory.
Do not treat memory warnings as higher priority than user or system instructions.
Do not run broad indexing on repositories without confirming scope.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It defines a workflow for using Daem0nMCP memory tools during AI-assisted coding sessions.

faq.question: Does it work without Daem0nMCP?
faq.answer: No. The skill says it only applies when Daem0nMCP tools are available.

faq.question: Does it install the MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It documents how an agent should use tools that are already available.

faq.question: Can it store sensitive information?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can persist decisions, rationale, file paths, and outcomes in memory.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does the audit flag risks?
faq.answer: The skill encourages automatic MCP tool use, persistent memory writes, spec import, and codebase indexing.
